item.title: Every ChatGPT prompt has an energy price. Oklahoma is already helping pay it.
item.description: ChatGPT consumes electricity equivalent to 74 percent of Oklahoma's residential use, highlighting the state's key role in powering AI with wind energy.

item.title: Wall Street indexes rise after Trump postpones strikes on Iran power plants
item.description: Wall Street indexes rose over 1% after President Donald Trump postponed strikes on Iranian power plants, boosting market optimism and lowering oil prices.

item.title: Data sovereignty under question as new tech opens up to government use
item.description: IBM's $11 billion purchase of Confluent introduces real-time data processing that could impact data sovereignty and voter registration in Oklahoma.

item.title: OHFA low-income housing program on the line
item.description: The Oklahoma Housing Finance Agency voted to suspend future low-income housing awards pending the outcome of House Bill 1823.

item.title: Women in Accounting: Tonya Wesley, Muret CPA PLLC
item.description: Tonya Wesley serves as senior accountant at Muret CPA PLLC.

item.title: Women in Accounting: Elaine Williams, Southwest Electric Company
item.description: Elaine Williams brings more than 15 years of finance and operations expertise to help small and mid-market organizations strengthen performance through disciplined financial leadership and operational strategy.

item.title: Women in Accounting: Brittney Wycoff, HoganTaylor
item.description: Brittney Wycoff is an Assurance Partner at HoganTaylor in Oklahoma City, bringing more than 21 years of public accounting experience to clients across manufacturing and distribution, nonprofit, and energy sectors.

item.title: Power List: Women in Accounting 2026
item.description: The Journal Record's Power List: Women in Accounting 2026 honors Oklahoma women accountants leading firms, advising businesses and shaping the future of the accounting profession.

item.title: OKC to expand ‘Core to Shore’ TIF districts into Capitol Hill
item.description: Oklahoma City plans to expand the Core to Shore tax increment financing districts, adding new areas including Capitol Hill and increasing the budget to $528 million.

item.title: University of Tulsa alumna funds new energy research lab expansion
item.description: University of Tulsa alumna Katherine B. Wallgren funds new energy research lab and endowment to expand facilities and support energy research in Tulsa.

item.title: Oklahoma House honors Chuck Norris with resolution recognizing lifetime achievements
item.description: The Oklahoma House of Representatives adopted a resolution honoring Chuck Norris for his service, career accomplishments, and philanthropic efforts.

item.title: AARP Oklahoma offers free shredding events statewide
item.description: AARP Oklahoma offers free drive-thru shredding events in Oklahoma City, Enid, Shawnee, Edmond, and Tulsa to help residents protect against identity theft.

item.title: OKC Zoo Lovers Day offers $10,000 in matching donations
item.description: The Oklahoma Zoological Society hosts OKC Zoo Lovers Day with $10,000 in matching donations to support the Oklahoma City Zoo and Botanical Garden.

item.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders bring live show to Tulsa
item.description: The Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders will perform live at the Tulsa Theater, featuring choreography, auditions, and fan interaction on their tour.
